claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions about your child (or children).

**First question: How old is your child?**

The eligibility rules depend on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally eligible (subject to other conditions)
- **16 to 19**: May be eligible if in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age (or the ages of all your children if you have more than one).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's very helpful.

So you have:
- **Alex, age 8**, who lives at home with you

Since Alex is under 16, that's a good start. Now let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old and lives at home with you, I assume he's not in paid employment, but I need to confirm this to continue the assessment properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just 8, so he's still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense - Alex is in primary school and not working at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

This refers to benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in his own name. At 8 years old, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm - is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name - he's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now the next check:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Again, given that Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely right! Alex is definitely not in an apprenticeship at 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important eligibility requirement.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit?**

You can qualify through ANY of the following ways:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common route)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with the right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do you normally live in the UK?** Or does one of the other situations apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK (in Manchester with Alex), so you meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now let's check responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You can show responsibility through ANY of these ways:

1. **You live with the child** (this is the most common)
2. You contribute to their upkeep (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you in Manchester. Is that correct - **do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you clearly meet the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check something important about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree on who should claim (and the current claimant would need to stop their claim first).

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, so we can continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- Is Alex currently **in hospital**?
- Is Alex currently **in care** (local authority care)?
- Is Alex currently **fostered**?
- Or is Alex living **normally at home** with you?

You mentioned Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, so I'm assuming it's the last option, but I need to confirm there are no special circumstances.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex was in care for a bit - a couple of months - but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. It's good to know Alex is back home with you now.

Just to clarify for the assessment: **Is Alex currently in care right now**, or is he living at home with you at this present time?

The assessment needs to know his current living situation. It sounds like he was in care previously but is now back home - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he was in care before, but he's living at home with me now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for clarifying! Alex is currently living at home with you now (not in care at the moment).

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now, one final question:

**Is the local council NOT currently paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council currently paying for Alex's living costs or upkeep? 

You mentioned he was in care before but is now back home with you. Is the council still contributing financially towards his accommodation or maintenance costs now that he's living with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex now - he's just living at home with me and I'm looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Excellent News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex. Based on our assessment:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - He's 8 years old (under 16), not working, not receiving benefits in his own right, and not in an apprenticeship  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives at home with you  
✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **No disqualifying factors** - The council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance  

---

### **Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?

Alex meets all the qualifying child criteria and the claimant meets all the eligibility requirements.
